title: A tick whose work is in another repository cannot be dispatched
description:
A tick whose work lives in ANOTHER repository cannot be dispatched.

`tk herd spawn` always creates a worktree of the repo whose tracker holds the
tick. Two ticks in this epic — 4l2 (retire the execution packages from ticks)
and 1ya (retire the factory from ticks) — do their work in the ticks checkout.
Dispatched from ticfac's tracker they get a ticfac worktree, the branch they
would need to touch is not there, and anything they changed in the ticks
checkout would be outside the worktree boundary: uncollectable and ungated.

Tick 4l2's worker diagnosed this itself and refused rather than reaching outside
its boundary, which is the correct behaviour and worth keeping.

This is not a ticfac bug today — it is a gap in what an orchestrator can
express. Options, to be decided:

- The tick declares its TARGET REPO, and the orchestrator creates the worktree
  there. The tracker stays where the work is planned; the worktree follows the
  code. Collect and the gate then have to run in that repo too, which is the
  real design question: whose gate proves a cross-repo change?
- Or cross-repo work is simply not dispatchable, and such a tick is marked as
  human-only from the start rather than discovered at dispatch. Honest, cheap,
  and it stops a worker burning a dollar to tell us what the tick already knew.
- Or the change is expressed as a PR against the other repo rather than a
  worktree edit — which is what a person would do anyway.

Whichever: a tick that cannot be dispatched should say so when it is PLANNED,
not when a worker reaches its boundary. That is the same principle as tick 01u
(a wave that cannot merge is refused at dispatch).
acceptance_criteria: A tick that targets another repository is either dispatchable into a worktree of that repository, with collect and the gate defined for it, or it is refused at PLANNING time rather than at the worker's boundary; the chosen shape is a logged decision; ticks 4l2 and 1ya are handled under it; no worker is dispatched to work it cannot reach.
